children: LVMH's fashion and leather goods sales fell 5% in the third quarter, missing analysts' expectations. The world's largest luxury group by sales blamed a worsening economic backdrop in China, particularly at the start of the quarter.

The French group's crucial fashion and leather goods division-home to brands including Louis Vuitton, Dior, Celine, Loewe and Fendi-generated EUR8.25 billion, equivalent to $9.2 billion, in revenue in the three months to September, below analysts' expectations of EUR8.39 billion. Overall, LVMH reported sales up 1% on an organic basis from a year earlier, helped by items such as watches and jewelry.

The performance of the fashion and leather-goods division, which analysts watch closely, underscores the difficulties facing a sector that relied for years on China's expanding middle class to drive sales of high-end handbags and clothing. A prolonged economic slowdown and weak consumer confidence have weighed on spending by Chinese shoppers, frustrating hopes of a sustained recovery in demand since the country emerged from Covid-era restrictions.

"Overall, these results confirm a stalling in already fragile recovery momentum from earlier in the year," analysts at RBC Capital Markets wrote in a note. LVMH shares have fallen about 40% since the start of the year.
